questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: How many amino acids are encoded by the human genetic code?
questions.explanation: The total number of standard amino acids encoded by triplet codons in the human genetic code is 20. Selenocysteine (Sec) in eukaryotes and pyrrolysine (Pyl) in prokaryotes are translationally inserted into proteins and are known as the 21st and 22nd amino acids respectively. Selenocysteine can be found in various human selenoproteins such as thioredoxin reductase, glutathione peroxidase, and deiodinases. In this question, 21 (20 standard AA + selenocysteine) is not provided as an option, so the correct answer would be 20.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: A neonate presents with feeding difficulty and failure to thrive. Her urine has a peculiar burnt sugar odor due to an excess of branched-chain amino acids. Which of the following is unlikely to be elevated?
questions.explanation: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). Lysine is not a branched-chain amino acid and hence is unlikely to be elevated. Branched-chain amino acids are valine, isoleucine and leucine. MSUD is due to deficiency of branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex, leading to formation of branched-chain amino acids and their toxic by-products (ketoacids) in blood and urine. There is a peculiar odor of burnt sugar found in urine, sweat, and cerumen.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is not an aromatic amino acid?
questions.explanation: Arginine is not an aromatic amino acid. The four aromatic amino acids, which include an aromatic ring, are phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan and histidine. Proline is a heterocyclic amino acid.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following amino acids has an imino ring?
questions.explanation: Proline is an amino acid with an imino ring. The distinctive cyclic structure of the side chain of proline gives it exceptional conformational rigidity as compared to other amino acids. Hence, proline plays a major role in collagen stability.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: A medical student was admitted to the hospital following a hunger strike. Which of the following amino acids cannot be used for gluconeogenesis by his body?
questions.explanation: Leucine cannot be used for gluconeogenesis. Leucine and lysine are the only purely ketogenic amino acids. These two amino acids yield only acetyl-CoA on oxidation (ketogenesis), and hence they cannot be used for gluconeogenesis. Four other amino acids give rise to both acetyl-CoA and intermediates and therefore can be used for both ketogenesis and gluconeogenesis: phenylalanine, isoleucine, tyrosine and tryptophan.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Out of the following, ______ is a semi-essential amino acid.
questions.explanation: Arginine is a semi-essential amino acid. Essential or indispensable amino acids are those that cannot be synthesized by the body and need to be supplied through diet. Semi-essential amino acids are those synthesized adequately by adults but synthesized at rates inadequate to support growth in children. Eight amino acids are absolutely essential, while two are semi-essential. The source includes a table classifying essential, semi-essential and non-essential amino acids.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following amino acids is not formed after post-translational modification?
questions.explanation: Selenocysteine, the 21st amino acid, is formed by co-translational modification rather than post-translational modification. It is encoded by the UGA codon, normally a stop codon. Selenocysteine can be found in human selenoproteins such as thioredoxin reductase, glutathione peroxidase and deiodinase. Selenocysteine is an analog of cysteine and is synthesized from serine. It plays an important role as cofactor in oxidation-reduction reactions; important human selenoproteins have roles in antioxidant, immunogenesis and atheroclerosis pathways and are associated with selenium-deficiency cardiomyopathy (Keshan disease).

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Amino acids absorb UV light due to _____.
questions.explanation: Amino acids absorb UV light due to aromatic rings. Aromatic amino acids such as tryptophan, tyrosine and phenylalanine absorb 250–290 nm UV light. The maximum absorption of UV light is by tryptophan. The source table shows: aromatic amino acids 250–290 nm (UV), nucleotides at pH 7 around 260 nm (UV), and porphyrins around 400 nm (Soret band, visible).

questions.explanation: Glycine is the smallest amino acid with R group as H atom. So, as it has no R group, it increases the flexibility of the protein. Proline and glycine are frequently found in beta turns.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is not a property of amino acids at isoelectric pH?
questions.explanation: The properties of amino acids at isoelectric pH are: maximum precipitability, minimum buffering action (note: maximum buffering action is when pH=pKa, and not at isoelectric pH), minimum solubility, and no mobility in an electric field.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: At physiological pH, buffering action in blood is caused by ______.
questions.explanation: At physiological pH, buffering action in blood is caused by histidine. The imidazole group of histidine has a pKa value of 6.5–7.4, which is close to physiological pH. Hence, histidine has the maximum buffering capacity at physiological pH.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: A mixture of insulin is being tested in a lab to determine its amino acid sequence. Which of the following reagents can be used?
questions.explanation: Sanger's reagent is used to determine the amino acid sequence. Peptides are isolated and hydrolyzed into a mixture of smaller peptides and treated with 1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (Sanger's reagent), which reacts with the alpha-amino groups of the amino-terminal residue. The amino acid content of each peptide is then determined, and the amino-terminal amino acid is identified.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: A forensic team performed a ninhydrin test on some samples obtained from a crime scene. This test can detect which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ninhydrin test is used to detect amino acids. A purple-colored complex (Ruhemann’s purple) indicates a positive reaction. Proline and hydroxyproline form a yellow adduct with ninhydrin. Glutamine and asparagine produce a brown color. This test is used effectively in crime scenes to develop and identify latent fingerprints.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: A neonate was incidentally diagnosed with a benign inborn error of metabolism. A positive Pauly's test would indicate the accumulation of which of the following amino acids in his urine?
questions.explanation: Pauly's test is used for detecting the presence of histidine in proteins. When proteins containing histidine react with diazotized sulfanilic acid under alkaline conditions, a red color is formed by a coupling reaction. The same reagent will give an orange colored product with the phenol group of tyrosine.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for the negative charge in fibrinopeptide A?
questions.explanation: Aspartate and glutamate are responsible for the negative charge in fibrinopeptide A and B of fibrinogen. The negative charges contribute to solubility of fibrinogen in plasma and importantly also serve to prevent aggregation by causing electrostatic repulsion between fibrinogen molecules.

questions.question: The graph shown below is the titration curve of a biochemical compound. Which of the following statement is true?

options.text: The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B
The points A and B represent the range of maximum ionization of the amine and carboxyl group
The compound has three ionisable side chains
The compound has one ionisable group

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B
questions.explanation: The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B, which correspond to pK1 and pK2 of the compound. The source notes that the points A and B represent the pKa of carboxyl and amino groups respectively; the amino acid has no ionizable side chain as the graph shows only two pKas; and it therefore has two ionisable groups, an amino group and a carboxyl group. The graph resembles the titration curve of glycine. The source further explains titration of glycine, buffering around each pKa, zwitterion behavior and that compounds with three or more pKas have an ionizable side-chain group.

questions.question: Nitric oxide is synthesized from:
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide is synthesized from arginine by a calcium-dependent reaction catalyzed by NO synthase. The co-enzymes of NO synthase include FMN, FAD, heme, and tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). The source includes the arginine → citrulline + NO reaction diagram.
